highlights.title: European tech stocks hit six-week low as calls for AI slowdown worry investors – business live
highlights.summary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news. AI-linked stocks fall after tech bosses call for slowdown in ‘reckless’ development. AI CEOs say they need to slow the pace of development. But will they? The Guardian view on controlling AI: humanity cannot outsource its survival.
body: Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.
Investors are reassessing the value of companies driving the artificial intelligence revolution after several leading AI figures called for a slowdown in development for safety reasons.

SoftBank, a major AI invester, fell by as much as 13% in Tokyo after OpenAI’s chief executive officer Sam Altman said that the ChatGPT-maker won’t go public this year (SoftBank owns a stake in OpenAI).
Traders’ optimism about AI has taken a hit after the CEO of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, appealed for the AI industry to “slow down” – a call which was quickly backed by both Altman and Elon Musk.

highlights.title: A multiplayer mod for The Last of Us 2 was reportedly cancelled "at Sony's request"
highlights.summary: Development on a multiplayer PvP mod for The Last of Us Part 2 on PC has been halted after PlayStation got in touch and asked the developers to cease work on the project.
body: "Hey everyone, as you all know, the [The Last of Us Part 2] multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month," wrote modder Speclizer in a post on social media. "Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you'll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own."

If you were curious about what the mod what have looked like in action, Speclizer uploaded about 25 minutes of gameplay for the mod back in June. You can see the video below. Given that the team has spent nine months working on the project, the legal request from Sony no doubt stings - but what did PlayStation's legal team seek out cancellation of this mods when there are so many others out there? It may be because the team behind this one would have added a paid component to the mod, funded by a Patreon account - something that tends to get unofficial mods shut down.

highlights.title: ‘I Like My Big Rat Wife’: Meet the People Using Chatbots to Write Custom Fiction
highlights.summary: While the publishing industry frets over how authors are using AI, many readers are taking things into their own hands.
body: When Petra Ferraz de Novaes isn’t at work, she’s probably lost in a fantasy crafted with the help of artificial intelligence.

Novaes, a 36-year-old software engineer from Brazil, has always loved storytelling. But making every little decision that goes into it—from style and syntax to character development—felt impossible. So in 2024 she asked an AI model to bring one of her ideas to life.

Novaes was delighted by the eccentric, sometimes wayward interpretations of her prompts, which carried the narrative in unexpected directions. “What fascinates me is the unpredictability,” Novaes tells WIRED. “People say that AI hallucinates a lot. But in this case, it’s probably what you want.”

These days, Novaes spends hours at a time building stories with AI, using a program called SillyTavern to run open-source models on her computer. She sketches out a concept—an elven warrior battles the queen of the Amazons and seizes her throne, for example—and watches the model fill in the gaps.

highlights.title: MIT spinout turns plastic waste into resilient building materials
highlights.summary: Atlas Building Composites is commercializing MIT research to turn plastic waste into parts for buildings and other infrastructure.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
The world needs more homes. The world also has too much plastic. Perhaps the only thing those two problems have in common is that they’re hard to solve.

Atlas Building Composites, a spinout of MIT, is on a mission to address both problems with a single solution. The company has developed an AI-powered robotic manufacturing platform capable of turning single-use plastics into durable building materials.

The company emerged from MIT HAUS, a research effort in the MIT Department of Mechanical Engineering that’s short for “Home Architecture for Universal Sustainability.” Atlas uses waterless plastic recycling and large-scale composite additive manufacturing technology to make parts like home foundations, decks, and trusses for walls, floors, and roofs.

highlights.title: Blizzard confirms no more Diablo 4 expansions from now until Diablo 5's release
highlights.summary: One of the biggest questions that emerged following the surprise reveal of Diablo 5 at BlizzCon over the weekend surrounded the future of Diablo 4. Blizzard announced a returning class - the Amazon - coming to the game sometime in the first half of 2027, but nothing beyond that.
body: Of course, the question on everyone's mind was whether the game will be getting any more expansions in the three-year wait between now and the 2029 release of Diablo 5. The studio's answer will likely disappoint many.

"We're all focused on [Diablo 4] seasons and getting to Diablo 5," Diablo game director Brent Gibson told PC Gamer. "We feel like we told the Story of Hatred. We had a great conclusion with Lord of Hatred with what we have with Mephisto, and we are moving towards telling the Story of Terror."

Lord of Hatred indeed had a great sense of finality, but I am willing to bet many simply saw it as the end of one arc rather than the game's entire story. Speaking of which, more story content is coming, but it will be delivered through upcoming seasons.

The events of Diablo 5 take place a century after Diablo 4 in a completely changed Sanctuary. It would have been nice to have a major Diablo 4 expansion serve as a narrative lead-in, but perhaps the 100-year gap is large enough to make that difficult. Still, Blizzard wants to do some of that work with seasonal content, but the developer doesn't quite know what shape things will take just yet.

highlights.title: Is it true that … having a hot drink will cool you down?
highlights.summary: A warm cup of tea can trigger sweating and lower your body temperature, but only if you’re in an airy space. Could a warm cup of tea really be the key to cooling down in hot weather?
body: Prof John Tregoning, the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death, says it depends on the circumstances. He points to the work of Australian scientist Prof Ollie Jay, who is a world leader in researching heat and how it balances out in your body.
When it comes to drinking a hot beverage, there are two effects on your body. “You’ve got the heat that the drink gives you, and then the amount that you sweat as a result of it,” Tregoning says.
While you’re consuming the warm drink, its high temperature will cause your body temperature to rise. That elevated temperature will trigger you to sweat more.
This is where things become complicated. Sweat cools down the body when it evaporates. When water on the skin turns to gas, it takes heat energy away from the body.

highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
body: As an AI-powered answer engine, Perplexity is deeply focused on search and accuracy. Its ability to process large amounts of information is critically important. Johnny Ho, Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, observes that every time the model gets better at writing code, Perplexity’s search engine improves too. It becomes able to write better programs that search the web and internal information and summarize it very concisely.
But the real challenge, according to Johnny, is taking those informational aspects and applying them to real-world systems. Something made easier with GPT‑6 Astra.
For Johnny, one of the most useful applications of AI is testing code. With limited time to test manually, he asks GPT‑6 Astra to build a small testing program around an application.

The model generates realistic responses like those another service would send, for example, a language model API or a connector. By standing in for those services, the model can check how the application responds and test the workflow from start to finish.

highlights.title: 'Pietersen will add spark' as he begins England white-ball coaching role
highlights.summary: Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.
body: Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.
"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."

highlights.title: 'Marvel’s Wolverine' Voice Actor Reveals Who Inspired His Take on Logan
highlights.summary: There’s no shortage of iconic Wolverine performances for actor Liam McIntyre to draw from. Hugh Jackman made Logan synonymous with his gruff, feral take on the character across the X-Men movies, while voice actors including Cal Dodd and Steve Blum have each put their own stamp on Marvel’s clawed…
body: Asked which previous versions of Wolverine inspired his performance, McIntyre gave a fairly definitive answer: all of them.

“It was every single one,” McIntyre said in an interview with Polygon while discussing his new animated series Golden Axe. “I had so many great teachers, from wonderful performance of the past, and trying to find your own sort of spin or take on it.”
For McIntyre, that meant looking at what made each previous interpretation of Logan work before figuring out how he could bring something of himself to the character.

“I would see Hugh [Jackman] and Cal Dodd and, Steve Blum and other wonderful performers and try to go, ‘Well, that’s such a great display of what makes Wolverine Wolverine. I’ll try and find the essence of that character as I can do it, because I can’t copy it,’” he said.

highlights.title: Burrata and beyond: a foodie tour of northern Puglia, Italy
highlights.summary: It’s the birthplace of the popular cheese, but the Barletta-Andria-Trani province in southern Italy has an array of local delicacies – from olive oil and yellow tomatoes to goat prosciutto. ‘I don’t eat mozzarella outside Puglia,” says our friend Savio.
body: Puglia is also the birthplace of ingredient du jour burrata, which originated in Andria, a few miles from Savio’s home town of Barletta. Andria forms one part of the triangular Barletta-Andria-Trani (BAT) province, often passed over for better-known parts of Puglia, despite the cheese connection and Barletta having miles of palm-backed, sandy beaches.

About a century ago, in the hills outside Andria, farmer Lorenzo Bianchino was snowed in and couldn’t get his milk to market. To save what he could, he revived an old technique for preserving butter ( burro, hence burrata), stuffing cream mixed with mozzarella scraps ( stracciatella ) in a casing of the stretched-curd cheese.

highlights.title: ‘We’re not going to back down’: tiny Dorset B&B stands up to Airbnb’s legal bid to ‘monopolise’ letters ‘bnb’
highlights.summary: Three little letters - bnb-side’s name is a play on the local b-side arts festival, but Silicon Valley colossus sees threat to global brand. In one corner is bnb-side, a six-room bed and breakfast on the Isle of Portland – a tiny wedge of limestone tied by a narrow ribbon of shingle to the Dorset…
body: On the other is Airbnb, the San Francisco-based booking colossus. The battle between them is over the three little letters they share.

b-side says the “bnb” in bnb-side means what it has always meant: bed and breakfast. But lawyers for the Silicon Valley titan say the name of the guesthouse, perched on an outcrop just 4 miles long by 1.5 miles wide, threatens the global brand of the $100bn heavyweight.

“We thought the name was both really obvious and really cool,” said Rocca Holly-Nambi, director of b-side. “b-side was founded almost 20 years ago, so when we set up our BnB in 2024 to raise money for the festival, we just popped the ‘bn’ in front because it’s a universally recognised description of what we’re offering.”

Airbnb doesn’t agree. In May, it sent the first of three legal letters to the tiny social enterprise to demand it cease its attempt to register the B&B using the name it had used since it opened its doors.

highlights.title: What’s behind the AI industry’s latest warnings of doom?
highlights.summary: On Equity, we discussed the AI industry's latest debate about whether it poses an existential threat to humanity.
body: The current discussion began after AI researcher Jacob Coxon said that he’s resigned from Anthropic because he’s worried that the leading AI companies are “gambling with our lives.” Then Anthropic’s alignment lead chimed in with a post declaring, “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” adding that he personally thinks the chance is “>10% within the next decade.”

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the latest apocalyptic warnings. I tried to articulate why I’m skeptical of many AI doomer narratives, while Kirsten asked if this was “just a weird way of flexing to show how far advanced their company’s AI model is,” particularly as these companies prepare to go public.

And Sean wondered how these concerns might show up in Anthropic’s S-1 filing for its IPO: “Are there junior lawyers right now who are going through and having to rewrite that entire section of the S-1 filing to say, ‘It’s a officially Anthropic’s position that there’s a more than 10% chance that we could develop something that would eradicate all of humanity and that would be materially bad for our business’?”

Lee debuted as a director with “Green Fish” in 1997, going on to build a filmography that also includes “Peppermint Candy,” “Oasis,” “Secret Sunshine,” “Poetry” and “Burning.” His work has drawn top honors on the festival circuit: “Oasis” earned him a directing prize at Venice in 2002, and “Poetry” took the screenplay award at Cannes in 2010. highlights.title: How Jane Wade Used Google AI For Her New York Fashion Week Show

body: After partnering with A24 to co-develop workflows for the film sector, Google’s Envisioning Studio set its sights on the fashion sector. Ahead of New York Fashion Week, Google partnered with designers Jane Wade and Sergio Hudson to develop and test two fashion-specific tools for pre-show styling and runway visualization in beta mode through its Flow AI creative studio.

“Our core premise is that technology must be built with creatives, not simply thrown over the wall at them,” says Yeawon Choi, the user experience designer within Google’s Envisioning Studio who led the project. “We co-design with the creative that will use these tools because we want them to be helpful. And across creative industries, from fashion to film, we’ve found similar friction points — all centering on pre-visualization, relentless timelines, and steep resource constraints.”

highlights.title: ‘Tidal wave’ of Pfas being launched to satisfy AI industry, campaigners warn
highlights.summary: Big manufacturers planning to produce more of the forever chemicals to meet demand from datacentres. Pfas companies are launching a “tidal wave” of forever chemicals production to meet demand from the AI industry, a campaign organisation has warned.
body: Despite alarm over the chemicals, which have been linked to cancer, a survey of the 10 biggest manufacturers found most had plans to increase production.
Many frame their investments around the “AI revolution”, because of the role Pfas play in semiconductor production and next-generation datacentre cooling systems.

But opponents warn that the chemicals, which never degrade in nature, are a ticking timebomb for human and planetary health. They say increased production risks undermining nascent moves to restrict Pfas in Europe, the UK and parts of the US.

“These companies’ expansion plans show that unless governments and regulators insist on a rapid phaseout, we will face a new tidal wave of forever chemicals,” said Anne-Sofie Bäckar, the executive director of ChemSec, the Swedish chemicals watchdog that carried out the research.

highlights.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards
highlights.summary: Obama recently said that Democrats need to make artificial intelligence one of their “central agendas” and “have a very clear plan” to address concerns around the technology’s economic impact and safety.
body: Obama made these comments on Thursday, at Democratic fundraising event where he was interviewed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. The NYT says that Obama’s office provided a partial transcript of the event, at which Jeffries asked Obama how congressional Democrats should approach AI.
In response, Obama said that once Democrats regain the House majority, they need to “put together a framework for a very public conversation.”

“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama added. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases.”

In a statement, Jeffries said the former president “is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence.” Jeffries also said that “Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people.”

highlights.title: South Korea pushes for football season to switch to winter after unbearable summer
highlights.summary: Why fainting fans and perspiring players are a worry for the Asian league seeking to follow Japan and align with Europe. South Korean football is trying to find the goldilocks time to play the K-League. Winters have long been too cold and, increasingly, summers are too hot.
body: Last week a survey revealed that more than 70% of 29 respondent coaches in Asia’s oldest professional league support a shift from the traditional March to November schedule to one that matches the European format, which starts in late August and has a winter break.

It is an old debate that has intensified of late along with the summer temperatures. The city of Yangsan reached 42.5 Celsius on 2 August, the highest since records began, and Seoul recorded 17 consecutive tropical nights, so defined when the temperature does not fall below 25 degrees.

Fans fainted in stadiums and coaches bemoaned the quality of play. It looks like it is only going to get worse. A December 2025 report from the Korea meteorological administration (KMA) found that temperatures in the country had risen 0.9 degrees from 2020 to 2024, a worrying amount given that the increase over the previous 100 years had been 1.9.

South Korea’s Pro Footballers Association (KPFA) called for a change. “The K League must transition … to protect players from the worsening climate crisis and punishing summer heat,” it said in a statement. “And to maintain the league’s leadership within Asia and its global competitiveness.”

body: Every overnight success has an origin story. Alan Ritchson 's just happens to include Simon Cowell.

Long before he was snapping bones as Jack Reacher, in 2004 Ritchson was a 20-year-old aspiring singer auditioning for American Idol, where he survived the contest long enough to charm Paula Abdul before eventually getting sent home. Good thing he turned out to be better at throwing punches than hitting high notes. A year later, he traded microphones for muscles, making his scripted acting debut as Arthur Curry, aka Aquaman, on Smallville.

Looking back now, it's easy to forget that Reacher wasn't the beginning of Ritchson's career, but it was the payoff. He spent nearly 20 years bouncing between network dramas, cult comedies, superhero shows, blockbuster franchises, and independent action films before finally landing the role that made him a household name. With Reacher season 4 coming to an end on Sept. 16, these are the 10 performances that stand above the rest.

body: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is Google’s fourth-generation folder and is still one of the only models with a full water and dust resistance rating similar to standard slab phones. It costs from £1,799 (€1,999/$1,899/A$2,799), which is £50 (€100/$100/A$100) more than last year as the pressure of RAMageddon continues to push up prices.

The 11 Pro Fold looks identical to previous models, but it is 19g lighter and fractionally slimmer in all directions with a slightly larger outside screen. Unlike Samsung’s slender Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra or squat models such as Apple’s iPhone Duo or the Galaxy Z Fold 8, the Pixel has the same ratio screen as Google’s slab phones and so handles precisely like them when shut with a bright and smooth 6.5in display.

Opened up, the internal screen is essentially square, which allows you to run two full-size apps side by side but is less ideal for video. The display is very bright, crisp and smooth, but the crease where it folds is more visible and detectable with your fingers than the best rivals. Like all foldable phones the screen is also delicate compared with standard hardened glass phones.

body: Miklosko joined West Ham from Baník Ostrava in 1990 for £300,000 after a trial and helped the club win promotion to the top division in his first season. He left in 1998 having made 373 appearances, joining QPR, initially on loan.

Miklosko ended his career at QPR in 2001 and returned to West Ham, where he worked as a goalkeeping coach until 2010. He later worked for a sports agency before taking roles at Baník Ostrava as a board member and sporting director.
West Ham said Miklosko would “forever hold a special place in the hearts of the West Ham family”. The club described him as a “beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man”.
Miklosko played 40 times for Czechoslovakia and twice for the Czech Republic in an international career that began in 1982. He said in 2024 that he was withdrawing from cancer treatment.

highlights.title: 9 Sci-Fi Series on Netflix That Are Perfect from Start to Finish
highlights.summary: But there are some shows on Netflix where this isn’t a problem and you can breeze through episode after episode without feeling like it's work to get back to the good stuff. Here are nine such sci-fi shows that are on Netflix right now, that are great from start to finish.
body: Far too often, when you’re watching a series on Netflix and you’re really getting into it, you reach a point where the show suddenly goes way downhill. (Or gets suddenly canceled with no notice.) Even if things improve again later, the lull messes with the overall experience. Stranger Things suffered a massive decline after season 3, while The OA ended on a massive cliffhanger.

Based on the book by Stephen King, 11.22.63 is an eight-episode miniseries about a time traveler trying to stop the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. Jake Epping (James Franco) is an ordinary English teacher tasked with the mission who ends up making all kinds of mistakes in the past, like getting too attached to the people there.

The show cleverly mixes classic sci-fi elements and themes and blends them with one of the best-known moments in American history, making the events and characters included take on a particular foreboding element. Especially interesting is the sense Jake gets that time itself is “pushing back” on his actions, as though what’s about to happen is supposed to happen and his mission may very well be hopeless.

highlights.title: Could Sabyasachi Be India’s First Global Luxury House?
highlights.summary: Sabyasachi Mukherjee makes his return to New York Fashion Week on Tuesday, 20 years after his last outing in the city. But this time, he is competing as a more mature luxury player.
body: The brand made its runway debut at Lakmé Fashion Week in Mumbai in 2002, with a collection called Kashgar Bazaar, focusing on Indian textile traditions in the form of Western shapes and Indian ensembles. It soon made the move into the big leagues, first in Milan and then in New York in 2006, where Mukherjee brought an artisanal collection called Snail, built around the idea of “slow fashion”, to the States.

That first New York outing came with a lesson: a label must be absolute at home before it can be truly international. It’s a high-stakes test for Indian fashion. No Indian designer has yet built a house with the scale, retail footprint, or cultural authority to compete as a genuine global luxury player.
Now, as he gears up to show in Tribeca this week, Mukherjee is betting he can be the first.
